name: Iseult of the White Hands

attributes.attribute: a Cornish or Breton heroine whom Tristan married after losing his fated lover Iseult
the hidden meaning of the duplicated name, linking Iseult to the goddess who chooses the king and Tristan's replacing of Mark

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Iseult of the White Hands is a Cornish or Breton heroine. After Tristan separated from his fated lover Iseult, he married another woman of the same name. Her happiness was short-lived. Tristan heard of the original Iseult's death. He pined away and died. The duplication of the name suggests a hidden meaning. It connects to the role of the original Iseult as a goddess of sovereignty. Tristan replaced Mark in the favor of the goddess. This suggests that the older man was no longer fit to rule as king.
